Three things I would tell anybody who is about to run their first public workshop, written down on the train home while the last one is still fresh in my mind.
Print the instructions
The projector will fail, the wireless will fail, and the one person who most needs the steps will be sitting behind a pillar. Paper works.
Finish early
Plan ninety minutes of material for a two hour slot. The spare half hour is not slack, it is where the questions happen, and the questions are the only part anybody remembers a month later. When I filled the whole slot I went home hoarse and the feedback forms said the session felt rushed, every single time.
Bring a second pair of hands
One of you talks while the other walks the room.
The walker sees the three people who fell behind at step two and are too polite to say so, and can fix it before step three makes it worse.
It also means somebody can fetch the extension lead without stopping the session.
